name: Greater Romania
summary: Greater Romania is the Romanian nationalist ideal of uniting all Romanians in one state, first realised in 1918 with Transylvania, Bessarabia and Bukovina and lost in part in 1940. Today it survives as irredentism toward Moldova and parts of Ukraine, most visibly in the Greater Romania Party. Adherents combine ethnic nationalism, Orthodox-tinged social conservatism, and a state-centred, populist approach to the economy.
scope: Greater Romania as the defining sources present it: the Romanian nation-state of 1918-1940 that united Transylvania, Bukovina, Bessarabia and the Banat with the old Kingdom and so 'encompassed the majority of Romanians' (Britannica), together with the nationalist ideal behind it, a state of all Romanians whose unity aspirations ran from the mid-19th century to 1918 (Chelaru), defined in ethnic terms in the interwar period (New Europe College proceedings). Its modern strand is the aim of reuniting Romania with the lost territories of Bessarabia and Bukovina, voiced by the Greater Romania Party and the New Right (Cinpoeş). Excludes the Iron Guard's fascist programme and the Antonescu regime as separate strands, and the 1918 resolution text, which no defining source names as the ideology's canonical document.
